IN.release_authority: Investigating officer of the cyber police station, or the jurisdictional Magistrate
IN.deadline_label: FairFreeze internal SLA: send a release memo within 72 hours (the SOP sets no fixed release time)
IN.notice_rule: Tell the customer the case number, the amount on hold, the police station, and that the rest of the account is usable. Do not share investigation details.

rules.source: I4C SOP for NCRP and CFCFRMS, 2 Jan 2026
rules.summary: Standard procedure for banks acting on cyber fraud requests raised through the national portal; Clause 10 gives account holders a grievance route.

rules.source: Kerala High Court rulings, 2026 (e.g. M.S. Kunnamangalam Co-operative Rural Bank v Inspector of Police)
rules.summary: Keep the account running and limit the lien to the amount in the police request, unless the bank itself suspects mule activity; the held amount stays for the Magistrate.
Police power to seize property suspected to be connected with an offence; a freeze must be reported to the Magistrate.

TH.regulator: Bank of Thailand / Anti Online Scam Operation Center (AOC 1441)
TH.release_authority: Bank, after AOC 1441 verification of the account holder
TH.deadline_label: Release within 4 hours to 1 working day once innocence is verified
allowed_legal_bases: พระราชกำหนด
อาชญากรรมทางเทคโนโลยี
ศูนย์ปฏิบัติการแจ้งความออนไลน์
TH.notice_rule: Notify by SMS or app: which amount is suspended, that other money is usable, and to call AOC 1441 (press 2) to verify. Do not share investigation details.

rules.source: Bank of Thailand and Thai Bankers' Association, Sept 2025
rules.summary: Suspend only the amount linked to the fraud case, not the whole account; notify the customer by SMS or mobile banking.
Unfreeze an innocent customer within 4 hours to one working day after verification through AOC 1441.

rules.source: Ministerial regulation under the Technology Crime Emergency Decree, in force 12 Aug 2026
rules.summary: Confirmed mule accounts lose mobile banking, ATM and online services across all banks; innocent holders must be separated from mules.

SG.release_authority: Police officer who issued the restriction order
SG.deadline_label: Restriction order lasts up to 30 days; police may renew it up to 5 times
SG.notice_rule: Explain kindly, in the customer's language, that the order protects them from a scam, that daily living money stays available, and how to ask the bank or police for help. Never blame the customer.

rules.summary: Police may order banks to restrict the banking transactions of a person believed to be about to send money to scammers, for up to 30 days, renewable up to 5 times.

rules.source: Protection from Scams Act 2025, legitimate needs
rules.summary: The restricted person can still ask the bank for money for legitimate needs such as daily living expenses.
